record.paper_title: Perspectivas sobre a Estatística de Extremos. Resultados básicos e problemas em aberto
record.original_question: For multivariate extreme-value statistics in dimension k, consider a k-dimensional random vector that is stable or is a limit law for componentwise maxima. After transforming each marginal distribution to the reduced Gumbel form, the joint distribution can be represented by a multivariate dependence function k(x2-x1, ..., xk-x1), subject to the validity conditions required for the resulting distribution. Its bivariate margins satisfy Boole-Fréchet-type inequalities, and independence of all bivariate margins is equivalent to mutual independence of all margins, which gives an independence test. Develop the largely open theory for this multivariate area, from model construction for such dependence structures to statistical inference and testing.

evidence.quote: Os raciocínios anteriormente feitos podem ser aplicados ao caso multivariado. Se for (X1,...,Xk) uma variável aleatória de dimensão k, estável ou limite para os máximos, a sua função de distribuição satisfaz as condições
A(x1, ..., xk) tem então a forma A(x1,..., xk) = exp{-[(e^-x1 +...+ e^-xk)] k(x2 - x1,..., xk - x1)} devendo a função k verificar as condições resultantes de ser A(x1,...,xk) > 0.
da qual decorre o resultado importante de que a independência das margens bivariadas é equivalente à independência mútua de todas as margens, o que permite um teste de independência.
Esta área só tem tido pequenos avanços estando praticamente em aberto, desde a modelização ao estudo estatístico.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X_1,\dots,X_k)$ be a $k$-dimensional random vector that is max-stable; equivalently, the distribution of componentwise maxima of i.i.d. copies, after affine normalization, converges to the law of $(X_1,\dots,X_k)$. Transform each marginal to the standard (reduced) Gumbel distribution $F(x) = \exp(-e^{-x})$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$, so that the joint distribution function $A(x_1,\dots,x_k)$ of the transformed vector has Gumbel margins. It is known that $A$ admits a representation of the form
$$A(x_1,\dots,x_k) \;=\; \exp\!\Big\{-\big(e^{-x_1}+\cdots+e^{-x_k}\big)\, k(x_2-x_1,\,\dots,\,x_k-x_1)\Big\},$$
where the "dependence function" $k:\mathbb{R}^{k-1}\to[0,\infty)$ must satisfy the constraints needed for $A$ to be a bona fide $k$-dimensional max-stable distribution function (in particular making all $k$ Gumbel margins correct and ensuring the appropriate complete-monotonicity / convexity conditions). Bivariate margins $A_{ij}$ of $A$ obey Boole–Fréchet-type inequalities, and pairwise independence of all bivariate margins is equivalent to mutual independence of $X_1,\dots,X_k$, yielding an independence test based on bivariate marginal dependence.

Develop a comprehensive theory for this multivariate setting:

(a) Characterize all admissible dependence functions $k(\,\cdot\,)$, i.e., give necessary and sufficient analytic conditions on $k$ so that the displayed formula defines a valid $k$-variate max-stable distribution with standard Gumbel margins.

(b) Construct flexible parametric and nonparametric families of such dependence functions for arbitrary dimension $k$, including hierarchical or factor structures.

(c) Develop statistical inference (estimation of $k(\cdot)$, asymptotic distribution theory of estimators) and goodness-of-fit and independence testing procedures, including the test based on the equivalence between pairwise and mutual independence of the margins, with explicit power and consistency analyses.
artifact.status_search_result: Multivariate extreme-value theory has seen substantial development since the original posing of this broad program. Characterizations of max-stable laws via spectral / Pickands / stable-tail dependence functions are well established (de Haan, Resnick, Pickands, Coles, Tawn), and many parametric families (logistic, Hüsler–Reiss, Brown–Resnick, max-linear) plus nonparametric estimators and tests of independence/asymptotic independence have been developed. However, the overall program—especially model construction, inference and testing in high dimensions—remains an active research area with many open subproblems, so the question as a whole is partially solved.

status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive treatment of multivariate extremes including dependence functions, models, and inference.
status_evidence.claim: Significant progress has been made on multivariate EVT models and inference.

status_evidence.title: Extreme Value Theory: An Introduction (de Haan & Ferreira)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops multivariate max-stable laws, spectral measure, and estimation.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization of multivariate max-stable distributions is established.

status_evidence.title: Statistical Modelling of Spatial Extremes
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Brown–Resnick and other max-stable processes with inference methods.
status_evidence.claim: Active ongoing research on multivariate/spatial extreme models and inference.
